name: compose_figure
title: Compose figure
description: Make a whole scientific figure on the server: a picture for each element, laid out with labels, arrows and a title, shown in the BioCartoon gallery with an editor link (an editable BioCartoon project), PNG/SVG downloads and credits. Pictures are catalog icons (each element's query is the plain name of the thing to depict) or the user's own: artwork you drew (svg), an image the user uploaded or generated in the conversation (image_file, with the file in the top-level image argument), or one at a URL. Use this, not a hand-made SVG, whenever the user wants a figure in BioCartoon. Prefer passing elements and connections you planned; a bare prompt is planned on the server. Read the returned match report: replace weak matches with a better query or an asset_id from search_assets, and treat placeholder boxes as gaps the library cannot fill. To edit a figure, pass its figure.spec back as `figure` with your changes (keep asset_id and image_ref on elements that should stay). Credit every catalog icon used. Not for charts of data.

prompt.description: What the figure should show, in words (used only when neither elements nor figure is given).

title.description: Title across the top. Omit for none.

layout.description: auto (default: grid without connections, cycle for one closed loop, hub when one element connects to all others, flow otherwise), flow (left to right), cycle, hub, grid.

id.description: Short id used by connections (e1, e2, ...). Default: e1, e2, ... in order.

label.description: Label printed under the picture (at most 60 characters).

query.description: 1–3 words naming the thing to find an icon for ("T cell", "mitochondrion", "lab mouse"). Default: the label.

asset_id.description: Use this exact catalog icon (from search_assets, or from a previous figure's spec) instead of searching.

placeholder.description: Keep an empty labelled box here (set by compose_figure when nothing fits).

svg.description: This element's picture as SVG markup you drew in this conversation (one complete <svg> with a viewBox; no scripts, external links or web fonts; up to 2 MB). Use instead of asset_id or query.

image_file.description: Use the conversation file (an image the user uploaded, or one generated in the chat) passed in that top-level argument as this element's picture.

image_url.description: An https URL of this element's picture (SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 2 MB).

image_base64.description: This element's picture, base64-encoded (a data: URL works too): SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 2 MB.

image_ref.description: The user's own picture from a previous figure's spec (compose_figure stores each one and returns this). Keep it when editing.

from.description: Element id (or label) the connection starts at.

to.description: Element id (or label) it points to.

kind.description: arrow (default), inhibit (flat bar head), double, line (no head), equilibrium, dashed (dashed arrow).

label.description: Short text beside the arrow ("activates", "secretes"), at most 40 characters.

sources.description: Draw icons only from these collections (one keeps a consistent style): bioart, bioicons, servier, scidraw, togotv, phylopic, healthicons, reactome, openmoji, noto, user.

name: open_in_biocartoon
title: Open in BioCartoon
description: A link that opens a figure (a compose_figure spec, which may include the user's own pictures), one catalog icon, or a shared template in the BioCartoon web editor as the user's own editable copy. The link is private (its key is in the fragment) and lasts 90 days after its last use.

name: export_figure
title: Export figure
description: A composed figure as one self-contained SVG file with its pictures embedded, for downloading only when the user asks for a file. Pass the figure.spec from compose_figure. To give the user a figure they can open and edit in BioCartoon, use compose_figure's editor link (or open_in_biocartoon) instead.
